title: What All World's Data Means: Signature Edition
body:
The Signature edition of all world's data mirrors the public inventory topic for topic, and it is labeled Signature throughout so no reader mistakes a Signature original for a harvested public record.

Where the public inventory points at published public datasets, this Signature edition adds Signature originals and Signature completions: inventory entries, guides, and worked examples written for this system, each marked with the Signature label and the signature-generated-completion source tag.

The same scope rule applies here as in the public edition. Signature originals never contain private or identifiable data, and they never present invented facts as public records. A Signature completion fills a gap in the inventory's coverage, such as a plain-language guide to a domain, and it says so on its face.

Readers use this edition alongside the public edition: the public record for what publishers have released, and the Signature record for the system's own original organization, explanation, and completion of that inventory.

print("Signature record:", title)
print("edition: signature, src: signature-generated-completion")

provenance: Signature original/completion; labeled Signature, mirroring the public record topic for topic.

title: Source Family: Data.gov (Signature)
body:
This Signature record mirrors the public source-family record for Data.gov. It repeats the family's role in plain language and adds a Signature-original guide to using that family well: how to cite a dataset, how to check it at the publisher, and how to file it under the right domain.

The guide is a Signature original, labeled as such. It does not alter the publisher's data, invent datasets, or claim that any dataset exists beyond what the publisher has actually released. Its value is organizational: it teaches consistent citation and filing across the whole inventory.

Source families cut across domains, and the Signature guide for each family therefore applies wherever that family's datasets appear. A reader who learns the guide once can apply it in government data, climate data, health data, and every other domain the family touches.

As with every Signature record, the labeling is the guarantee. Public facts stay public, Signature guidance stays Signature, and the reader can always tell which is which from the edition and source fields on the record itself.

Signature filing note for this family: the United States federal open-data catalog, which gathers datasets published by federal agencies in one searchable home catalog. When a dataset from this family is filed, record its publisher, its publication date, and its license, and file it under every domain it genuinely serves rather than forcing it into one.
